answer: History-gated action quota is the mechanism. A kernel scheduler grants each new identity a small action budget, refilled only by confirmations from distinct counterparties over separate time windows. A clone must spend the full cost of generating a unique history at zephyr pace and waiting out every window before gaining scale. Comet-like bursts or repeated counterparty patterns merge or freeze the clone, so honest identities keep quota while mass cloning loses value.
